name: Cuihu Green Lake
tagline: Willow-lined lake district next to Yunnan University
description: The prettiest central pocket of Wuhua District, wrapped around a lake park where retirees dance at dawn and gulls arrive each winter. Narrow surrounding streets hold hostels, coffee roasters, tea houses and student bars. It is the default base for foreigners and the easiest place in Kunming to work from a cafe.
bestFor: Nomads who want cafes, a park and a walkable core without renting a car.
pros: Lake park on the doorstep for breaks
Walk or metro to most of central Kunming
cons: Rents run above the Kunming average
Tour groups crowd the lake at weekends
Older buildings, thin walls and weak heating in winter

name: Nanping Street and Dongfeng
tagline: The commercial heart of downtown Kunming
description: Kunming's main shopping and business core, built around the Nanping pedestrian street and the Dongfeng Road corridor. Department stores, malls, hotels and office towers sit on top of two metro lines. Serviced apartments here suit anyone who wants everything within a few blocks and no commuting.
bestFor: Short-stay workers who want maximum convenience and metro access.
pros: Two metro lines and every bus route
Serviced apartments easy to book short term
cons: Loud traffic on the main roads

name: Guandu District
tagline: An old temple town swallowed by the modern southeast city
description: Home to the restored Guandu Ancient Town with its stone pagodas and snack lanes, surrounded by newer residential blocks and the road to the airport. Rents drop noticeably compared with downtown and Line 1 of the metro runs through. Good value for anyone staying a couple of months.
bestFor: Budget-focused nomads staying a month or more who want a local Chinese neighbourhood.
pros: Clearly cheaper rents than the centre
Handy for the airport and long-distance buses
cons: Few Western-style cafes to work from
Ancient town gets packed with day trippers

name: Xishan and Dianchi Lakeside
tagline: Newer lakeside towers under the Western Hills
description: The southwest belt where Kunming meets Dianchi Lake, with recent high-rise compounds, waterfront promenades and the Western Hills park rising behind. Flats are modern with better insulation and lifts than the old centre, and weekend hiking starts at the door. Public transport is thinner than downtown.
bestFor: Remote workers who want a newer flat, fresh air and weekend hiking nearby.
pros: Modern apartments with lifts and better heating
Lake and hill walks minutes away
Cleaner, quieter air than the centre
cons: Longer commutes into the city core
Dianchi water quality is still poor in places

name: Beichen and North Panlong
tagline: Quiet northern residential blocks near the botanical gardens
description: A settled residential belt north of the centre around Beichen, with big produce markets, a large shopping complex, ordinary Chinese apartment compounds and easy access to the Kunming Botanical Garden and Golden Temple park. Metro Line 2 links it to downtown in about twenty minutes.
bestFor: Longer-stay nomads who want a calm local base with real markets and lower rent.
pros: Calm streets and cheap fresh markets
Metro Line 2 straight into the centre
Parks and hills easily reachable to the north
cons: Very few cafes suited to laptop work
Feels far from the centre without the metro
